text:
anya_support: Heads-up: Acme SRE opened an escalation — their app in account A cannot reach our hosted Redwood API via the interface endpoint in account B. Getting intermittent 403s then timeouts. They say this started after a change to a central firewall ALLOW list earlier today. Can someone jump in?

samir_eng: Do we know if this is an AWS Interface Endpoint (com.amazonaws...) or a cross-account PrivateLink NLB?

anya_support: It's an Interface VPC Endpoint (vpce-0abc1234) created in the shared services account (B). Consumer account (A) is using shared hosted zone for endpoint DNS. Customer logs: repeated TLS handshake failures, then connection reset.

ryan_infra: Can you get me a dig +trace from the consumer app host and a curl -v to the endpoint DNS name? Also need SGs attached to the VPCE and the consumer subnet route table.

jess_csm: I already asked them to run basic checks. They pasted this: 
```
$ dig private-redwood.acme.internal +short
10.0.64.12
$ curl -v https://private-redwood.acme.internal/health
* Connected to 10.0.64.12 (10.0.64.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection established
* SSL certificate: CN=api.redwood.internal
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\n\n```
They also tried from a bastion in the same subnet and got timeouts.

samir_eng: 403 then timeouts suggests something between endpoint and backend rejecting, then a firewall/NAT exhaustion causing drops. Did they change egress allowlist on their central firewall today?

anya_support: They said yes — added a small IP set rule to only allow traffic from their outbound NAT IPs and the VPCE IP range. They mention they also rotated a managed rule for the firewall.

ryan_infra: Two quick pitfalls to look for with cross-account interface endpoints:
- DNS resolving to the wrong AZ/ENI (private hosted zone association mismatch)
- Endpoint SGs that reference the wrong CIDR or expected ENI tags
- Central firewall ALLOW lists that whitelist old NAT IPs but not the new ENI outbound IPs

samir_eng: Ask them for `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=attachment.instance-owner-id,Values=vpce` output (ENI IPs) and the firewall ALLOW list entry.

jess_csm: They returned the ENI listing and firewall rule:
```
ENIs on vpce-0abc1234: 10.0.64.12 (subnet-a), 10.0.128.11 (subnet-b)
Firewall allowlist: 54.22.11.0/24, 54.22.12.0/24  (old NAT pool)
```
Consumer subnet nat-gateway egress IPs are 54.33.99.7 now (new nat).

anya_support: Aha. So the firewall is only allowing the old NAT IPs. But why the 403s earlier?

ryan_infra: Two possible reasons co-occurring: the request from the consumer subnet to the VPCE ENI hits the interface endpoint SG which expects traffic from the consumer VPC CIDR (or from specific SGs). If the endpoint SG was tightened to only permit source SGs that belong to account B, cross-account traffic may be rejected (403 at app layer) or rejected earlier. Another is the DNS resolving to a different ENI that then gets routed through firewall and dropped.

samir_eng: Also check the endpoint's private hosted zone association. If the consumer account's VPC wasn't associated correctly, their DNS might resolve to a stale target (e.g., a decommissioned ENI in another AZ).

jess_csm: They ran `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name` and `associate-vpc` looks OK. But I asked them to run `nslookup private-redwood.acme.internal <100.96.0.2>` from the pod and paste the full resolution chain.

(10 minutes pass)

jess_csm: Pasted: `private-redwood.acme.internal -> 10.0.64.12 (AZ a)`, but when they traceroute that IP from the bastion it goes through the central firewall public IP then times out.

ryan_infra: That indicates their route for that subnet is sending traffic to an egress appliance (transit/NGFW) for inspection. If the NGFW doesn't allow the NAT IPs for the ENI or the endpoint-backed flow, packets are dropped. The initial 403 seen earlier might have been our service rejecting malformed/mutated TLS from an inline proxy, then after they tightened rules it started dropping entirely.

samir_eng: What's our recommendation to customer to quickly confirm?

anya_support: Ask them to: 1) SSH into a host in the consumer subnet and curl the ENI IP directly with -k and -v, 2) Temporarily add the ENI private IPs (10.0.64.12, 10.0.128.11) to the firewall allowlist, 3) check the VPCE SG rules to ensure it allows traffic from consumer VPC CIDR or SG.

jess_csm: They did step 1 and 3. curl -vk to the ENI IP returned same TCP connect then immediate RST from our side sometimes, and nothing other times. They updated firewall allowlist to include 10.0.64.12 and 10.0.128.11 and *that* immediately fixed connectivity from the bastion -> endpoint (no more timeouts).

ryan_infra: Great smoke test. So root cause: central firewall was blocking traffic to the VPCE ENI addresses (they had only whitelisted NAT pool and not the VPCE ENI private IPs). Two concurrent effects: partial responses (403) when proxy mutated TLS or forwarded via a different NAT path, and timeouts when NGFW dropped flows entirely.

samir_eng: Can we make a permanent fix recommendation?

anya_support: Recommend:
- Add a stable tag-based allowlist on their NGFW that references the VPCE ENI IPs (or better, tag their VPCE ENIs and have an IP-set automation)
- Ensure endpoint security group allows source SG or the consumer VPC CIDR (for cross-account) instead of hard-coded IPs
- For shared hosted zones, verify each consumer VPC has the correct association and TTLs are low while debugging
- Add an observability check: quick endpoint-health probe from consumer account after any firewall change

jess_csm: They want a note to pass to the firewall team. I'll send the summary and include the commands we used.

support-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0345 — Temporary fix applied (firewall allowlist updated for ENI IPs).

anya_support: Follow-up action items for us: 1) add a KB doc for cross-account interface endpoint troubleshooting (DNS -> ENI IPs -> firewall allowlist) 2) label this case as "egress-allowlist-caused-timeouts" so Solutions can find similar cases.

ryan_infra: I'll draft the KB and include a small script to fetch ENI IPs and print suggested firewall rules:
```
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters "Name=description,Values=*vpce-*" --query 'NetworkInterfaces[*].PrivateIpAddress' --output text
```

samir_eng: Also call out that managed proxies/firewalls that do TLS inspection can cause valid TLS to appear invalid (403) if they truncate or mangle SNI/certs. When possible, allow passthrough for private endpoints.

jess_csm: Customer confirmed they reverted the ALLOW-list change and instead automated IP-set with the VPCE ENIs. They reported steady success and no further 403s. Closing on their side.

anya_support: Thanks all. I'll update the support ticket with timeline and mitigation steps.

support-bot: Thread archived after 7 days of inactivity.
